questions.q: Two bodies are projected with the same velocity. If one is projected at an angle of 30° and the other at 45° to the horizontal, then the ratio of maximum heights attained is [Figure: a projectile trajectory launched at an angle above the horizontal, reaching a peak height]
questions.explanation: Maximum height H ∝ sin²θ, so the ratio = $\sin^2 30^\circ/\sin^2 45^\circ = (1/4)/(1/2) = 1:2$.

questions.q: In the projectile motion of a particle on a level ground, which of the following remains constant with reference to time and position?
options: Vertical component of the velocity of the projectile
Average velocity between any two points on the path
Angle between the instantaneous velocity with the horizontal
questions.explanation: In projectile motion there is no horizontal acceleration, so the horizontal component of velocity stays constant throughout the flight.

questions.q: A particle is in uniform circular motion. The equation of its trajectory is given by (x − 2)$^2$ + y$^2$ = 25, where x and y are in meter. The speed of the particle is 2 ms$^{-1}$. When the particle attains the lowest 'y' co-ordinate, the acceleration of the particle is (in ms$^{-2}$)
questions.explanation: Radius $=5$m, centre $(2,0)$. At the lowest point $(2,-5)$ the centripetal acceleration $a=v^2/r=4/5=0.8\,ms^{-2}$ directed towards the centre, i.e. along $+\hat j$.

questions.q: An athlete runs along a circular track of diameter 80m. The distance travelled and the magnitude of displacement of the athlete when he covers $\dfrac{3}{4}^{th}$ of the circle is (in m)
questions.explanation: Distance $=\dfrac34\times2\pi r=\dfrac34\times2\pi(40)=60\pi\,m$; displacement (chord subtending $270^\circ$) $=\sqrt2\,r=40\sqrt2\,m$.

questions.q: Among the given pair of vectors, the resultant of two vectors can never be 3 units. The vectors are
questions.explanation: The resultant of two vectors P and Q always lies between $|P-Q|$ and $P+Q$; for 4 and 8 units this range is 4 to 12, which excludes 3.

questions.q: A particle is in uniform circular motion. Related to one complete revolution of the particle, which among the statements is incorrect?
options: Displacement of the particle is zero.
Average speed of the particle is zero.
Average velocity of the particle is zero.
Average acceleration of the particle is zero.
questions.explanation: Average speed = distance travelled/time = circumference/T, which is nonzero; so the statement that average speed is zero is incorrect.

questions.q: Two objects are projected at an angle $\theta$ and (90$^\circ$$-\theta$), to the horizontal with the same speed. The ratio of their maximum vertical heights is
questions.explanation: $H=\dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$, so $\dfrac{H_1}{H_2}=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^2(90^\circ-\theta)}=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\tan^2\theta$.

questions.q: The maximum range of a gun on horizontal plane is 16 km. If g = 10 ms$^{-2}$, then muzzle velocity of a shell is
questions.explanation: Maximum range $R_{max}=\dfrac{u^2}{g}$, so $u=\sqrt{R_{max}\,g}=\sqrt{16000\times10}=400$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The trajectory of a projectile is
options: a parabola in the absence of air resistance
questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, a projectile follows a parabolic path; with air resistance the path deviates from a parabola.

questions.q: For a projectile motion, the angle between the velocity and acceleration is minimum and acute at
questions.explanation: Acceleration is constant (vertically downward). The vertical component of velocity changes steadily from +u sin$\theta$ (upward, at launch) to -u sin$\theta$ (downward, at landing) while the horizontal component stays fixed, so the angle between velocity and acceleration decreases monotonically over the flight and is smallest only at the single instant of landing.

questions.q: A particle starts from the origin at t = 0 s with a velocity of 10$\hat{j}$ ms$^{-1}$ and moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration of (8$\hat{i}$ + 2$\hat{j}$) ms$^{-2}$. At an instant when the x-coordinate of the particle is 16 m, the y-coordinate of the particle is:
Rain is falling vertically with a speed of 12 ms$^{-1}$. A woman rides a bicycle with a speed of 12 ms$^{-1}$ in east to west direction. What is the direction in which she should hold her umbrella?
questions.explanation: Velocity of rain relative to woman $=(12\text{ east},\,12\text{ down})$, i.e. it appears to come from $45^\circ$ on the west side of vertical, so she must tilt the umbrella $45^\circ$ towards the West.

questions.q: The trajectory of a projectile projected from origin is given by the equation $y = x - \dfrac{2x^2}{5}$. The initial velocity of the projectile is
questions.explanation: Comparing with $y = x\tan\theta - \dfrac{g x^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$: $\tan\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 45^\circ$, and $\dfrac{g}{2u^2\cos^2\theta} = \dfrac{2}{5} \Rightarrow u^2 = \dfrac{5g}{4\cos^2 45^\circ} = \dfrac{5\times9.8}{2} \approx 25 \Rightarrow u \approx 5$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The angle between velocity and acceleration of a particle describing uniform circular motion is
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, velocity is tangential and acceleration (centripetal) is radial, so they are always perpendicular (90°).

questions.q: If $\vec A = 2\hat i + 3\hat j + 8\hat k$ is perpendicular to $\vec B = 4\hat j - 4\hat i + \alpha \hat k$, then the value of 'α' is
questions.explanation: $\vec A \cdot \vec B = 0 \Rightarrow 2(-4) + 3(4) + 8\alpha = 0 \Rightarrow 4 + 8\alpha = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: Three projectiles A, B and C are projected at an angle of 30°, 45°, 60° respectively. If $R_A$, $R_B$ and $R_C$ are ranges of A, B and C respectively, then (velocity of projection is same for A, B & C)
questions.explanation: Range $R \propto \sin(2\theta)$: $\sin60°=\sin120°=0.866$ and $\sin90°=1$, so $R_A=R_C<R_B$.

questions.q: The component of a vector $\vec r$ along x-axis will have a maximum value if
options: $\vec r$ makes an angle of 45° with the x-axis
questions.explanation: The x-component is $r\cos\theta$, which is maximum ($=r$) when $\vec r$ is along the +x axis.

questions.q: A particle is projected with a velocity v so that its horizontal range is twice the greatest height attained. The horizontal range is
questions.note: The standard answer is $4v^2/5g$: R = 2H gives tan\theta = 2, so sin\theta = 2/\sqrt5, cos\theta = 1/\sqrt5, and R = (v^2/g)\sin2\theta = 4v^2/(5g); the KEA key marks option (1) $v^2/g$, which does not satisfy R = 2H.
questions.explanation: For R = 2H: tan$\theta$ = 2, which gives R = $4v^2/5g$ by standard projectile-motion derivation, but KEA's key marks option (1) $v^2/g$ as correct.

questions.q: The ratio of angular speed of a second-hand to the hour-hand of a watch is
questions.explanation: The second hand completes a revolution in 60 s, the hour hand in 12 h = 43200 s; ratio of angular speeds = 43200/60 = 720 : 1.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Potential energy is a scalar quantity, while nuclear spin (angular momentum), weight and momentum are all vectors.

questions.q: A stone is thrown vertically at a speed of 30 ms$^{-1}$ making an angle of 45$^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. What is the maximum height reached by the stone? Take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$.
A projectile is projected at 10 ms$^{-1}$ by making at an angle 60$^\circ$ to the horizontal. After some time its velocity makes an angle of 30$^\circ$ to the horizontal. Its speed at this instant is
questions.explanation: The horizontal velocity component $v_x=10\cos60^\circ=5\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ stays constant throughout the flight. When the velocity makes 30$^\circ$ with the horizontal, $v_x=v\cos30^\circ$, so $v=5/\cos30^\circ=10/\sqrt3\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.

questions.q: The X and Y components of a force F acting at 30° to the x-axis are respectively
questions.explanation: $F_x = F\cos30° = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}F$ and $F_y = F\sin30° = \dfrac12F$.

questions.q: The height $y$ and the distance $x$ along the horizontal plane of a projectile on a certain planet (with no surrounding atmosphere) are given by $y = 8t - 5t^2$ meter and $x = 6t$ meter, where $t$ is in seconds. The velocity with which the projectile is projected is .................
questions.explanation: $v_x = 6$ ms$^{-1}$ and $v_y = dy/dt = 8-10t$, so at $t=0$, $v_y = 8$ ms$^{-1}$; the initial speed is $\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The resultant of two forces acting at an angle of $120^0$ is 10 kg wt and is perpendicular to one of the forces. That force is .................
questions.explanation: If resultant $R$ is perpendicular to force $P$, then $P+Q\cos120^0=0 \Rightarrow Q=2P$; using $R^2=P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos120^0=3P^2$, $P=R/\sqrt3=10/\sqrt3$ kg wt.

questions.q: A boy throws a cricket ball from the boundary to the wicket-keeper. If the frictional force due to air cannot be ignored, the forces acting on the ball at the position $X$ are represented by ..................... [$X$ is a point early in the ball's rising, forward path from the boy towards the wicket-keeper; each option is a small force-arrow diagram]
options: [two arrows from a common point: one pointing down-and-to-left (opposite the ball's forward velocity), one pointing straight down]
[two arrows at right angles from a common point: one pointing right, one pointing straight down]
[two arrows from a common point: one pointing up-and-to-right (along the direction of motion), one pointing straight down]
[a vertical double-headed arrow, one pointing up and one pointing down]
questions.explanation: At $X$ the ball moves up and forward, so gravity acts vertically down while air drag acts opposite to the velocity (backward along the path); these two forces (drag down-and-to-left, gravity straight down) match option 1 (as per KEA key).
